liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playing In The Band** (2 reviews): Playin' and I Know You Rider are described as hot; Donna wails at the start and again at the end of a long Playin' [12][17]
- **Loser** (1 review): Loser is lively and fiery despite the mix problems [7]
- **Candyman** (1 review): A jaunty Candyman where the show turns special; reviewer values hearing this version from the Midwest 1972 run [6]
- **The Other One** (1 review): A roughly 29-minute Other One with Weir on wah-wah, Phil popping thumb notes, and nice rhythm from Keith [12]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Stella Blue has exceptionally sweet vocals from Jerry, giving the listener goosebumps [14]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Ramble On Rose has Garcia's vocals recorded so intimately that he seems to be singing in the room [16]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 other source): This source repairs a dropout in Brokedown Palace [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-11-22.sbd.fixed.miller.115765.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 177 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: Fades that followed most tracks in earlier versions were dealt with; disc changes are seamless [1]
- **gd72-11-22.sbd.lai.4081.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 180 min; rated 4/5 by 16 [3]. Said about its sound: First-set mix has problems at the start of Sugaree, mostly settling by Beat It On Down The Line; Billy's drums sound distant for most of the show, though the recording is warm and roomy; Mix problems affect the first set [6][7][10][13]
- **gd1972-11-22.115730.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 177 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1972-11-22.141189.sbd.menke.lee.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: soundboard; 25 songs; 180 min [4]

## Around the show

- Mentions a San Jose 1972 show with a far more Weir-heavy mix [10]
- Compared with Houston as a favorite; shorter than other '72 barnburners, and the band never really speeds up [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-11-22.sbd.fixed.miller.115765.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Reel Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [1]. Also: Fixed Miller transfer from a DAT supplied by David Gans; the Brokedown Palace dropout is repaired [1]
- **gd72-11-22.sbd.lai.4081.sbeok.shnf**: source: sdb> master reel> dat> cdr [3]
- **gd1972-11-22.115730.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Reel Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [2]
- **gd1972-11-22.141189.sbd.menke.lee.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Menke and Pat Lee; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Matt Smith; source: Master Soundboard Reels > Bob Menke's 1st generation reels > Pat Lee's 2nd generation reels (dolby b decoded) [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Concertposterauction.com: [Grateful Dead Austin Municipal Auditorium 1972 Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/1485199/Grateful-Dead-Austin-Municipal-Auditorium-1972-Concert-Poster) [20]
- Fan art by Concertposterauction.com: [Grateful Dead Austin Municipal Auditorium 1972 Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/1485199/Grateful-Dead-Austin-Municipal-Auditorium-1972-Concert-Poster) [21]
